| # Emergency (EMCY) {#emergency-emcy-1 .p_Heading1 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}                                                                                                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                                                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

The Emergency Message (EMCY) is a service, which signals internal fatal device errors to inform other CANopen devices in the network. The error types are defined in the communication profile and the device profiles. The EMCY is transmitted with the highest priority.

The CANopen defines EMCY producer and EMCY consumer. The producer transmits EMCYs and the consumers receive them.

The EMCY telegram consists of 8 bytes. It contains an emergency error code, the contents of object [1001h](object-0x1001-error-register.html){.topiclink}, and 5 bytes of manufacturer-specific error code. Each transmitted error code and the first two bytes of the manufacturer-specific code will be pushed in the predefined error field on index [1003h](object-0x1003-pre-defined-erro.html){.topiclink}. This field can contain up to 255 error entries. The value of sub-index 0 shows the current number of entries. The most recent occurred error will be always inserted on the top of this field (sub-index 1). All older entries will be moved down.

The Emergency message is sent with CAN-ID 0x80h+Node-ID. The Emergency telegram is structured as follows

 

+---------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CAN-ID        | Data                                                                                                                                                                     |
|               +--------------+--------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+--------------+--------------+--------------+--------------+--------------+
|               | Byte 0       | Byte 1       | Byte 2                                                          | Byte 3       | Byte 4       | Byte 5       | Byte 6       | Byte 7       |
+===============+==============+==============+=================================================================+==============+==============+==============+==============+==============+
| 0x80h+Node-ID | Emergency Error Code        | Error Register\                                                 | Manufacturer Specific Error                                              |
|               |                             | (Object [1001h](object-0x1001-error-register.html){.topiclink}) |                                                                          |
+---------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+

 

If there are no more errors on the device, an EMCY with error code 0 will be sent as shown in the table below.

 

  CANID           Data
  --------------- ---------------------------------
  0x80h+Node-ID   00h 00h 00h 00h 00h 00h 00h 00h

 

 

## Emergency Error code: {#emergency-error-code .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

 

  Error Code (hex)   Meaning
  ------------------ ---------------------------------------
  00xx               Error Reset or No Error
  10xx               Generic Error
  20xx               Current
  21xx               Current, device input side
  22xx               Current inside the device
  23xx               Current, device output side
  30xx               Voltage
  31xx               Mains Voltage
  32xx               Voltage inside the device
  33xx               Output Voltage
  40xx               Temperature
  41xx               Ambient Temperature
  42xx               Device Temperature
  50xx               Device Hardware
  60xx               Device Software
  61xx               Internal Software
  62xx               User Software
  63xx               Data Set
  70xx               Additional Modules
  80xx               Monitoring
  81xx               Communication
  8110               CAN Overrun (Objects lost)
  8120               CAN in Error Passive Mode
  8130               Life Guard Error or Heartbeat Error
  8140               Recovered from bus off
  8150               Transmit COB-ID collision
  82xx               Protocol Error
  8210               PDO not processed due to length error
  8220               PDO length exceeded
  90xx               External Error
  F0xx               Additional Functions
  FFxx               Device specific
